member.name: T:NCMapper.Attributes.AfterMappingAttribute
member.summary:
Post-mapping lifecycle hook attribute — applied to a DTO class to invoke a static callback method after the mapping operation completes (i.e., after all property assignments).
Usage: [AfterMapping(typeof(OrderMappingHost), nameof(OrderMappingHost.Enrich))] or locally annotated as [AfterMapping(nameof(Enrich))] (method declared on the DTO itself).
Functional equivalence: This attribute populates the same snapshot-backed field as the Fluent pipeline’s terminal .AfterMapping(...) method. Previously, this field was accessible only via the Fluent API; the attribute-based approach now provides compile-time emission (whereas runtime registration was previously available only via per invocation).

remarks.para: Method contract: The target method must be public or internal static (within the same assembly) and have signature void M(TSource source, TTarget target), where TSource/TTarget correspond to the source type specified by [MapFrom] and the DTO type itself. Resolution failures (e.g., method not found, inaccessible, signature mismatch, or overload ambiguity) trigger compile-time diagnostics NCMAP038/039/040.

Execution timing: Executed after the main mapping flow completes—including BeforeMapping preprocessing and all property assignments—but before the mapping method returns. Applies also to record/constructor-integrated targets (invoked after construction—unlike BeforeMapping, which is prohibited for such targets per diagnostic F37).

Coexistence with AddPostMap: This attribute (compile-time emission) and (runtime per-invocation registration) may coexist. Execution order is: generated AfterMapping → pipeline PostMap. During migration from AddPostMap to this attribute, users will observe duplicate execution—due to fundamentally different mechanisms (compile-time emission vs. runtime registration). Migration requires explicit removal of legacy registrations.
Inheritance: Inherited = false — derived DTOs do not inherit the hook and must declare it explicitly (consistent with [MapTree] semantics).

Projection: IProjectionPolicy.RequiresDowngrade = true — ORM projections (where nested projections skip generated code, causing hook omission and semantic failure) are forcibly downgraded to in-memory mapping (full semantics).

Scope: Hooks are bound per DTO (target-level) and activated per mapping pair based on method signature match. A hook fires only for mapping pairs (TSource, TTarget) whose signatures match the declared method (including purely Fluent-declared pairs injected across pairs via propagation). Non-matching pairs emit no hook and generate no diagnostics.

member.name: T:NCMapper.Attributes.MapSubclassAttribute
member.summary:
Polymorphic subclass registration attribute — applied on the base-class DTO that carries [MapFrom], explicitly registering a subclass mapping pair for the base-class mapping (Scheme 1: type-level multi-instance annotation on the base-class DTO).
Usage: [MapFrom(typeof(Animal))] [MapSubclass(typeof(Dog), typeof(DogDto))] [MapSubclass(typeof(Cat), typeof(CatDto))] class AnimalDto { ... } — mirrors the Fluent API terminal .For<TSource, TTarget>().MapSubclass<TSrcDerived, TTargetDerived>() (both channels are equivalent, sharing the P-f engine). Expressiveness asymmetry (D-n principle): attribute arguments are typeof constants without compile-time generic constraint enforcement — inheritance relationship violations trigger NCMAP_F46 at compile time (Fluent side uses CS0311/CS0314 for interception).

remarks.para: Inheritance Blocking: Inherited=false — derived DTOs do not inherit subclass registrations from their parent (blocked at runtime via reflection; Roslyn symbol analysis naturally prevents propagation at compile time — confirmed in O-1 Spike Q1 testing).

Dispatch Semantics: Shared with the Fluent side — compile-time isinst dispatch chain (assignability-based matching; deepest unregistered descendant matches the nearest registered ancestor) + most-derived-first arbitration + base-class fallback; covers all four families: Map, _Update, MapList, and MapListInto (Update and MapListInto perform dual-instance matching — destination type is fixed).

Static-type key spaces are naturally bounded and behaviorally stable. Dynamic types rebuild property dictionaries on every access (direct computation), preserving semantic equivalence with cached paths (mapping result conservation), avoiding eviction/rebuild concerns.

For test isolation involving the same type pair, use unwarmed scenarios or process-level isolation.
